01 · Executive Summary

July delivered strong revenue at ₹17.97L net — above the 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) average, with improving trial conversion and rising churn as the key watchpoints.

Headline revenue closed at ₹17.97L net (₹18.89L gross, ₹1.76L discount), which is +31.2% vs Jun 2026 (M-1), +26.2% vs May 2026 (M-2), +23.2% vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul), and +14.5% vs Jul 2025 (YoY). Trial conversion is 24.8% (38 of 153 trials), up +1.6pp MoM. Churn rate stands at 26.8%, deteriorating +5.3pp MoM. Discount efficiency is ₹10.72 of revenue collected per ₹1 discounted.

Executive Strategic Analysis — July 2026
Strategic Analysis & Action Plan

July’s growth is strong, but member retention and underused capacity will determine whether the improvement becomes repeatable.

💡 What the Numbers Mean — in Plain English (5)
  • 💡
    Revenue Growth Driven by Volume
    The studio's impressive revenue growth of 31.3% was largely volume-driven with transactions increasing by 24.2%. This indicates a successful pull strategy attracting more customers; however, the relatively small increase in ATV suggests untapped potential in upselling strategies. (₹18,89,427 gross (+31.3%) from 231 transactions (+24.2%) while ATV rose just 5.7%)
  • 💡
    High Churn Rate Signals Retention Opportunity
    A churn rate of 26.8% indicates significant membership turnover which is well above healthy industry standards (<3%). This presents an opportunity to focus on retention programs that could stabilize member count and enhance long-term revenue stability. (Churn rate at 26.8%, net member change -71)
  • 💡
    Lead Conversion Below Benchmark
    Lead conversion rates are currently at 11.8%, significantly below the healthy benchmark of 30-45%. Improving this metric could dramatically boost the pipeline efficiency without additional marketing spend. (Lead conversion rate at 11.8%, compared to baseline of ~12%)
  • 💡
    Class Fill Rates Indicate Capacity Utilization Gap
    With class fill rates averaging only 41.6%, there's considerable room to improve capacity utilization through targeted promotions or schedule adjustments designed to attract more attendees during underutilized slots. ('Class fill rate at 41.6%' against baseline of ~44%)
  • 💡
    'Momentum Deceleration Across Key Metrics'
    Revenue is rising faster than attendance, fill rate, and member retention. In simple terms, a smaller group of higher-spending clients is carrying the result. The studio should protect that value while rebuilding the buyer base and improving repeat attendance.
🎯 Actionable Recommendations (1)
  • 🎯
    Revamp Class Scheduling Strategy
    Analyze attendance patterns to adjust class timings or formats that better match member availability.
    🎯 Expected Impact: Increasing fill rates above current levels can significantly boost session profitability.

Key Insights · July 2026
01
Revenue at ₹17.97L net (+23.2% vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul)) — Volume-Driven Lift.
Net sales sit at ₹17.97L (+23.2% vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) average of ₹14.58L, +31.2% vs Jun 2026). Transactions (231) and ATV (₹8,179) reveal the growth engine.
What this tells us: Top-line momentum is active, but discounting (9.3% penetration) is eroding margin yield.
Strategic Action: Pivot from price discounting to value-add bonuses to stabilize ATV and recover ~₹1.1L/mo in net margin.
02
Trial conversion rate at 24.8% (+6.0pp vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul)) — Strong Conversion.
38 of 153 trialists converted (24.8%), +1.6pp vs Jun 2026 and 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) average of 18.8%.
What this tells us: The trial experience is effectively convincing prospects to join.
Strategic Action: Expand lead acquisition spend on high-converting channels.
03
Churn at 26.8% (+6.1pp vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul)) — Retention Leakage.
Of 71 expiring memberships, 43 renewed (60.6%), while 19 lapsed (26.8% churn).
What this tells us: Lapses are escalating among members with declining check-in frequency in month 3.
Strategic Action: Set automated alerts when a member visits fewer than 3 times in 30 days to trigger coach check-ins.
04
Discount Efficiency at ₹10.72 per ₹1 Discounted — Margin Healthy.
Discounts total ₹1.76L against ₹18.89L gross (9.3% penetration) vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) efficiency of ₹6.96.
What this tells us: Promotional offers are yielding adequate net sales return.
Strategic Action: Maintain current pricing controls.
05
Fill Rate at 41.6% across 284 Sessions — Utilization Signal.
284 sessions generated 1,516 visits (avg 5.3/session), -1.2pp vs Jun 2026 vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) average of 42.2%.
What this tells us: Prime slots are running near capacity while off-peak hours pull down overall facility utilization.
Strategic Action: Reallocate low-fill off-peak hours to peak class formats to unlock ~40 incremental visits per week.
06
Lead Volume at 220 Leads (+19.4% vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul)) — Pipeline Health.
Lead volume sits +37.5% vs Jun 2026 vs 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) average of 184. Top source: Hosted Class (78 leads, 1 converted).
What this tells us: Lead acquisition is generating steady prospect volume.
Strategic Action: Scale ad spend on top-performing acquisition channels.
07
192 Late Cancels (4 Heavy Cancelers) — Capacity Loss.
Late-cancel rate is 11.2% of check-ins (-1.3pp vs Jun 2026), with 4 members canceling 5+ times. Zero penalty collected.
What this tells us: Unenforced cancellation policies result in wasted spot capacity and prevent waitlisted members from attending.
Strategic Action: Implement a standard ₹250 late-cancel fee to recover lost spots and improve class commitment.
08
Bandra is the group’s #2 engine: 34.0% of July gross.
₹18.89L of the group’s ₹55.58L July gross came from Supreme HQ — behind Kwality House (₹25.80L, 46.4%) and ahead of Kenkere House (₹10.88L).
What this tells us: The flagship’s playbook (Strength Lab sell-outs at 80–89% fill) is a portable, proven playbook Bandra hasn’t adopted yet.
Strategic Action: Import the Strength Lab category and the flagship’s trial-close protocol in August.
09
Growth quality check: price-led, not people-led.
Unique buyers fell to 168 (-13.0% YoY vs 193) and transactions to 231, while ATV rose to ₹8,179 (+13.4% YoY).
What this tells us: A smaller, richer base is carrying the month — strong pricing power, but a structural exposure if returning spend softens.
Strategic Action: Track unique-buyer count as a weekly health metric alongside revenue.
10
Returning clients closed a quarter of the month.
Three Studio Annual Unlimited closes to returning clients: ₹4.85L = 25.7% of all sales (all at 20% off via SHQ20).
What this tells us: Renewal moments — not acquisition events — are where big tickets close.
Strategic Action: Make the annual-upgrade conversation a scripted step at every 3-month expiry.
11
Pipeline optics outrun pipeline truth.
220 leads looks strong, but hosted channels supplied 78 of them (35.5%) for just 2 conversions (~2.5%), 41 leads sit parked at “Trial Completed”, and 134 CRM records marked “Membership Sold” hold ₹0 of revenue.
What this tells us: Net of the noise, the effective pipeline is far smaller than reported.
Strategic Action: Reconcile CRM stages to POS and re-mix channels toward referral/WhatsApp (26–44% conversion).

The July balance sheet — what worked vs. what didn’t

A two-column read of the month, drawn from the sales, session, funnel, churn and instructor deep dives. Wins to protect on the left; leaks to fix in August on the right.

What worked in July
✓
Late-cancel discipline transformed
Late cancellations fell from a catastrophic 32.6% of bookings (Jul 2025) to 11.2% — wasted spots slashed, waitlists actually clear, booking predictability restored.
✓
The package pivot monetises every mat
Class Packages +71.9% YoY to ₹8.41L and revenue per visit up +58.6% to ₹832 — fewer visits, but each one paid and package-backed.
✓
High-intent closing muscle works when used
Calls, referrals and WhatsApp convert at 26–44% with ₹37–₹53K tickets, and three renewal-window annual closes banked ₹4.85L.
✓
Payment-mix discipline is real margin
Stripe held to 15.4% of sales at 2.89% (₹8.4K fees); bank transfer + cash carried 79%+ fee-free — ~₹46K of processing margin kept in July.
What didn’t work in July
✗
The post-trial exodus deepened
Only 38 of 153 first visits returned (24.8%), and CRM trial-to-conversion collapsed to 18.6% vs 52.2% last July — the single largest growth leak in the studio.
✗
Hosted pop-ups filled rooms with non-buyers
78 hosted leads (35.5% of pipeline) → 2 conversions; 5 pop-up events hosted 45 first-time trialers with zero purchases — prime slots spent on free-trial seekers.
✗
Recurring base is weakening
Membership revenue -20.9% YoY, member share of check-ins down to 62.4% (-12.6pp), and 59.8% of historical newcomer 2-for-1 contracts lapsed after class #2.
✗
Empty rooms and a missing category
16 sessions ran empty (5.63% of schedule, up from 2.17%) and Bandra carries zero Strength classes despite flagship sell-outs at 80–89% fill.

Revenue Quality & Mix Analysis — July 2026
Composition, pricing power & margin leaks
📋 Detailed Revenue Narrative

July’s top line is genuinely strong on the surface — ₹18.89L gross (+31.3% MoM; ₹17.97L net) — but its quality is shifting. Growth is price-led, not people-led: the buyer base shrank to 168 unique buyers (-13.0% YoY) and transactions fell to 231 (-10.5% YoY), while average transaction value climbed +13.4% YoY to ₹8,179. Structurally, the studio is pivoting from recurring memberships (-20.9% YoY) to bulk class packages (+71.9% YoY) — excellent for cash this month, weaker for predictability next quarter. Three returning-client annual closes (₹4.85L, 25.7% of sales) single-handedly carried the wholesale story, while Stripe discipline kept processing fees to ₹8.4K. The one number that can rewrite this entire report is the applied GST rate (18% → 5%), flagged in the compliance note below.

💡 What the Numbers Mean — in Plain English (5)
  • 💡
    Growth is price-led, not people-led
    Gross recovered +31.3% MoM and net is +14.5% above Jul 2025, yet the client footprint contracted — buyers and transactions are both ~10–13% below last year. A smaller, richer base is doing the lifting. (buyers 168 vs 193 YoY; txns 231 vs 258 YoY; ATV ₹8,179 (+13.4% YoY))
  • 💡
    The package pivot: cash now, predictability later
    Class Packages exploded +71.9% YoY to ₹8.41L (45% of revenue) while Memberships fell -20.9% YoY to ₹8.46L and single-class drop-ins collapsed -50.9%. Bulk prepay flatters this month’s P&L but erodes recurring revenue visibility. (packages ₹8.41L / memberships ₹8.46L / singles ₹1.06L (-50.9% YoY))
  • 💡
    Three annual closes carried the month
    Three Studio Annual Unlimited Memberships generated ₹4.85L — 25.7% of all sales — every one to a returning client at 20% off (code SHQ20, ₹1.16L total discount). Renewal moments are the real revenue engine. (3 × Annual Unlimited @ ₹1.62L avg; all returning clients)
  • 💡
    Seller concentration is acute — and Imran fell off a cliff
    Deesha Changwani drove ₹5.84L across 65 transactions (30.9% of studio sales) with Shipra Bhika at ₹3.76L, while Imran Shaikh crashed -45.2% YoY from ₹6.00L to ₹3.29L across 35 transactions. (top 2 sellers = 51% of attributed sales; Imran -45.2% YoY)
  • 💡
    Payment discipline saved ~₹46K; the tax rate is the big open question
    Stripe was contained to 15.4% of sales at a 2.89% fee (₹8.4K) — bank transfer + cash (79%+) carried the rest fee-free. Meanwhile VAT collections dropped -67.9% YoY after the applied rate shifted 18% → 5% in 2026. (Stripe ₹2.91L @2.89% = ₹8.4K fees; VAT ₹2.82L → ₹0.91L YoY)

Pipeline & Trial Conversion Analysis — July 2026
Record volume at the top; a collapsing close at the trial desk
📋 Detailed Funnel Narrative

The funnel’s surface reads beautifully — 220 leads (+37.5% MoM), a record ~188 monthly conversions, and 153 first visits (+50.0% MoM). Underneath, the machine is breaking: the trial-to-conversion rate collapsed to 18.6% (23 of 124 CRM triallers) from 52.2% a year ago, the average lead now takes 44.8 days to convert (+67.6% YoY), and the value of an in-month conversion crashed to ₹1,483 (-85.8% YoY). Hosted pop-up events are inflating the pipeline optics — 78 hosted leads (35.5% of total) produced only 2 conversions, and 45 hosted first visits produced zero. Meanwhile high-intent channels (calls, referrals, WhatsApp) convert at 26–44% with ₹37K–₹53K average tickets but get a fraction of the attention. Two hygiene items poison the read further: 41 leads parked at “Trial Completed” and 134 ghost “Membership Sold” records with ₹0 of purchases.

💡 What the Numbers Mean — in Plain English (6)
  • 💡
    Trial-to-conversion collapsed to 18.6%
    Only 23 of 124 triallers bought anything after class, versus a 52.2% close rate last July. 4 out of 5 people who experience the studio never pay it a rupee. (23/124 (18.6%) vs 48/92 (52.2%) in Jul 2025)
  • 💡
    Record conversions, hollow value
    Total conversions hit a record (~188 — leads closed in-month from any cohort), but their average LTV crashed to ₹1,483 (-85.8% YoY): the team is closing volume on the cheapest products. (₹1,483 vs ₹10,461 in Jul 2025; -38.5% MoM)
  • 💡
    The pipeline has slowed to 44.8 days
    Average conversion speed worsened +67.6% YoY (26.7 → 44.8 days) — follow-ups are happening weeks after intent cools. (44.8-day average lead-to-close cycle)
  • 💡
    Hosted events are an illusion of demand
    78 hosted leads (35.5% of pipeline) yielded 2 conversions (~2.5%); across 5 July pop-ups, 45 first-time trialers produced exactly zero purchases. (Physique 57 × Payal Sewani, BPB, Mum Tribe, Reena Chhabra, Renu Saraf: 0/45)
  • 💡
    High-intent channels are starving
    Enquiry-on-call converts at 44.4% (per template read; deep-dive 33%, ₹44.7K avg), client referrals 27.8% (₹37.4K) and WhatsApp 26.3% (₹53.0K) — yet they represent a minority of sales effort. (referral 18 leads → 5 conv; WhatsApp 19 → 5; calls 9 → 3)
  • 💡
    CRM hygiene is masking the true queue
    41 leads sit stuck at “Trial Completed” with no active follow-up, and 134 leads marked “Membership Sold” show ₹0 purchases and ₹0 LTV. (134 ghost records understate real pipeline work by ~2 weeks)

🔄
Floor Economics & Schedule Efficiency — July 2026
The revenue paradox: fewer visits, richer visits
📋 Detailed Sessions Narrative

July produced a genuinely paradoxical floor: session revenue ₹12.62L (+31.8% YoY) on -16.9% fewer check-ins (1,516) across 284 sessions (-12.1% YoY). Value per visit jumped to ₹832 (+58.6% YoY) — the package pivot monetises every mat — but the schedule is stretched thin at 41.6% fill, underfilled formats (Mat 57 Express 14.6%, Back Body Blaze 27.0%, Cardio Barre 27.8%, Trainer’s Choice 28.6%) drag the average, and 16 sessions ran completely empty (5.63% of schedule), more than double last year’s 2.17% rate. The loudest signal is structural: Bandra runs 84 Cycle + 200 Barre sessions and zero Strength classes, while Kwality House’s Strength Lab sells out at 80–89% fill. Late-cancel discipline is the stand-out operational win — down from 32.6% to 11.2% of bookings YoY.

💡 What the Numbers Mean — in Plain English (6)
  • 💡
    Fewer, richer visits: the revenue paradox
    Session revenue +31.8% YoY on -16.9% attendance because every visit is now paid and package-backed. (₹12.62L vs ₹9.57L YoY; 1,516 vs 1,825 check-ins; ₹832/visit (+58.6%))
  • 💡
    Empty-room payroll leak more than doubled
    16 sessions (5.63% of the schedule) ran with zero clients, up from 7 (2.17%) last July — direct payroll and utility loss on rooms that never opened. (16/284 sessions empty; Anmol alone holds 4 empty sessions)
  • 💡
    Underfill is concentrated and fixable
    Four formats run under 29% occupancy (Mat 57 Express 14.6%, Back Body Blaze 27.0%, Cardio Barre 27.8%, Trainer’s Choice 28.6%) while Express/FIT formats run 60–79%. (PowerCycle Express 78.9% fill; Studio FIT 59.8% (263 check-ins, ₹2.20L))
  • 💡
    The missing Strength category
    Bandra scheduled 84 Cycle and 200 Barre sessions but zero Strength; the flagship’s Strength Lab is its top category at 80–89% fill — proven, portable demand. (0 Strength sessions in Bandra in Jul 2026 (and Jul 2025))
  • 💡
    Barre 57 remains the volume anchor
    378 check-ins across 59 sessions, contributing 23.9% of session revenue (₹3.01L) at a moderate 45.8% fill — valuable headroom on a safe format. (Barre 57 = ₹3.01L of ₹12.62L session revenue)
  • 💡
    Membership attendance share is slipping
    Members drove 62.4% of check-ins (-12.6pp YoY) while packages rose to 28.9% (+13.3pp) — useful cash now, a harder-to-forecast base next quarter. (62.4% vs 75.0% member share of check-ins, Jul 2025 vs Jul 2026)

Retention & Risk Intelligence — July 2026
More than half the active base is in the danger zone
📋 Detailed Retention Narrative

Bandra’s July expiration book was small (71 memberships: 43 renewed, 19 lapsed, 9 frozen), but the structural readings are the most alarming in the group. Historically, 39.2% of all 7,438 resolved contracts lapsed; in the current active register, 78 clients are high-risk and 24 medium-risk — 52.6% of the 194 active base. The behavioural signature is precise: lapsed clients averaged 2.15 completed sessions vs 5.72 for renewals, risk peaks at the 7th-class milestone (10 actives stuck there), and the primary flag is attendance of just 0.5–0.8 classes/week. The powerful counterweight: price elasticity — discounted contracts renew at 74.5% vs 58.8% full-price (+15.7pp) — and the product ladder’s anchor, 1-Month Unlimited, renews at 79.4% historically.

💡 What the Numbers Mean — in Plain English (6)
  • 💡
    52.6% of the active base is at risk right now
    78 high-risk + 24 medium-risk of 194 active clients — the highest exposure in the group. This is the leading indicator behind July’s 26.8% churn print. (78/194 high (40.2%), 24/194 medium (12.4%))
  • 💡
    The under-3-classes cliff
    Lapsed clients completed just 2.15 sessions on average before churning vs 5.72 for renewals — below 3 classes, a package is a countdown, not a habit. (2.15 vs 5.72 avg completed sessions; risk frequency 0.5–0.8 classes/week)
  • 💡
    The 7th-class milestone is the trigger point
    Ten active clients sit exactly on class #7 — novelty fades, scheduling fatigue bites. Milestone-timed outreach beats generic check-ins. (10 of 194 actives stuck at the class-7 milestone)
  • 💡
    The Newcomer 2-for-1 trap
    59.8% of 749 historical newcomer contracts lapsed after using their two classes — and 37 more clients bought the same product this July. (749 contracts: 40.2% renewed / 59.8% lapsed)
  • 💡
    Renewals are price-elastic — discounts are medicine here
    Discounted contracts renew at 74.5% vs 58.8% full-price (+15.7pp). A targeted 10% loyalty offer costs margin but saves accounts. (74.47% vs 58.76% renewal by discount status)
  • 💡
    Seller-linked churn: closing quality, not just quantity
    Akshay Rane’s clients renew at 91.1% (101 contracts) and Jimmeey Gondaa’s at 89.0% (109), while Nadiya Shaikh’s book renews at only 58.4% (397) and Saniya Makwana’s at 63.4% (191). (Nadiya 397 contracts at 58.4% — the largest low-quality book)
Exclusions applied in this section (per management guidance): zero-value memberships, ‘Newcomers 2 For 1’ SKUs, ‘Studio Single Class’ SKUs, and all Private-class memberships. Complimentary / referral-free / influencer-free / staff-family classes are also excluded (zero LTV). The cleaned table below covers only revenue-bearing memberships where the lapse represents real lost revenue.

Active risk profile — where the churn is incubating

Risk is behavioural and visible weeks before lapse: attendance frequency, milestone proximity and cancellation habits. The register below sizes the tiers across the 194-strong active base.

Trigger signals
01
Frequency is the #1 flag: 0.5–0.8 classes/week.
High-risk actives attend under once a week — below the 3-session activation threshold within any fortnight window.
What this tells us: The habit never forms at this cadence.
Strategic Action: Instructor spotlight + same-day WhatsApp check-in when a flagged client attends.
02
The 7th-class milestone is the largest single trigger (10 actives).
Clients stall exactly where novelty fades and scheduling fatigue sets in.
What this tells us: Milestone-timed nudges outperform generic blasts.
Strategic Action: Class-6 trigger: goal-setting note + class-8 booking assistance at the desk.
03
Under-3 classes = countdown, not habit.
Historic lapsed clients averaged 2.15 completed sessions vs 5.72 for renewals.
What this tells us: The first fortnight decides the contract’s fate.
Strategic Action: “Quick Starter” rule: 3 classes in 14 days, rewarded with a recovery shake + grip socks.
04
Cancellation hygiene feeds the risk model.
Late-cancel and no-show behaviour clustered with eventual lapses; July’s improved 11.2% late-cancel rate (from 32.6% LY) is a genuine leading win.
What this tells us: Protect the cancellation policy gains — they correlate with retention.
Strategic Action: Keep the automated waitlist + late-cancel fee live; review the 4 heavy cancelers individually.

Value at stake — the August bridge

Every lever is priced from July’s own data.

Reporting conventions: Net Sales excludes taxes; Gross Sales reflects amount billed per transaction. Comparators — M-1 = Jun 2026, M-2 = May 2026, 2026 Avg (excl. Jul) = Jan–Jun 2026 mean, YoY = Jul 2025. All ₹ figures are Indian Rupees; L = lakh (₹100,000). Session revenue is class-attributed net revenue. Behavioural risk tiers use attendance frequency, cancellation rate and class-milestone proximity on the active client register. Funnel metrics appear in three lenses (retention view, CRM-strict view, new-client registers) — each is labelled where used.
A · Commercial & Revenue Metrics
MetricHow it is calculatedWhat it tells the business
Net SalesΣ transaction revenue excluding GST. July: ₹17.97L (+31.2% vs Jun; +14.5% YoY).The studio’s true trading topline — every comparator in this report is computed on Net Sales.
Gross SalesΣ billed transaction value incl. tax, net of discount. July: ₹18.89L.Headline demand captured at the desk; the gap to Net Sales is the tax line.
Discount ValueΣ promotional value given. July: ₹1.76L (+37.5% YoY).How much list price was conceded to close the month.
Discount PenetrationDiscount ÷ gross = ₹1.76L ÷ ₹18.89L = 9.3%.Margin discipline gauge; red-flag threshold > 10%.
Discount EfficiencyNet sales ÷ discount value = ₹17.97L ÷ ₹1.76L = ₹10.72 per ₹1.Whether promotions earn or burn — lower means paying more for each rupee closed.
TransactionsCount of settled invoices: 231 (-10.5% YoY vs 258).Volume engine of the P&L; falling transactions on rising revenue = price-led growth.
Average Transaction Value (ATV)Gross ÷ transactions = ₹18.89L ÷ 231 = ₹8,179 (+13.4% YoY vs ₹7,215).Basket size — July’s savior; Bandra’s affluent base buys bigger packs.
Unique BuyersDistinct purchasing clients: 168 (-13.0% YoY vs 193).Breadth of the active paying base — the report’s quiet alarm.
Returning vs New SpendReturning-client average spend ₹15,204 (+22.0% MoM); new-client average first purchase ₹9,569 (+17.2% YoY).Where the money sits: renewal moments and big-ticket base spend, not acquisition.
Revenue / VisitSession-attributed revenue ÷ check-ins = ₹12.62L ÷ 1,516 = ₹832 (+58.6% YoY).Monetisation per mat — the package pivot’s clearest win.
Category Revenue MixCategory net sales ÷ total. July: Memberships 45% · Class Packages 45% · Sessions 6% · Newcomers 4% · Retail 1%.Mix health — the shift from contracts to packs weakens forecastability.
Seller AttributionNet sales credited per seller. July: Deesha ₹5.84L (30.9%), Shipra ₹3.76L, Imran ₹3.29L (-45.2% YoY); top-2 = 51%.Closing concentration — who the month depends on.
Payment Mix & FeesChannel share of sales: Custom/bank 55.5% (₹10.48L), Cash 23.6% (₹4.47L), Stripe 15.4% (₹2.91L) × 2.89% = ₹8.4K fees.Fee leakage — holding cards near 15% saved ~₹46K in July.
B · Sessions & Utilisation Metrics
MetricHow it is calculatedWhat it tells the business
Sessions HeldScheduled classes delivered: 284 (-12.1% YoY vs 323; +7.2% MoM).Capacity supplied to the market; contracted for demand.
Checked-in VisitsAttended bookings from class registers: 1,516 (-16.9% YoY; +4.2% MoM).Real floor traffic feeding every utilisation metric.
Fill RateCheck-ins ÷ bookable capacity = 41.6% (vs 44.0% LY; threshold < 37%).How much of each room is earning; the schedule’s core efficiency read.
Average Class SizeVisits ÷ sessions = 1,516 ÷ 284 = 5.3.Class energy and payroll-per-head economics.
Late-Cancel RateLate cancellations ÷ bookings = 11.2% (192 cancels; 32.6% in Jul 2025).Booking discipline — July’s biggest behavioural win.
Empty SessionsSessions with zero check-ins: 16 = 5.63% of schedule (vs 2.17% LY).Direct payroll/utility leak on rooms that opened for nobody.
Format FillPer-format occupancy. July: PowerCycle Express 78.8% · Studio FIT 59.8% · Barre 57 45.8% · Mat 57 Express 14.6%.Which formats sell out (clone) vs stagnate (prune).
Session RevenueNet revenue attributed to classes: ₹12.62L (+31.8% YoY; +10.5% MoM).The floor’s earning power and instructor payroll pool.
Peak Slot / Day TotalsArgmax of the day × slot grid. July: 18:00 Thu, 66 visits; busiest day Saturday 278; weekend = 26% of demand.Where capacity is binding — anchor instructors/closers there.
C · Funnel & Acquisition Metrics
MetricHow it is calculatedWhat it tells the business
LeadsNew CRM leads created: 220 (+37.5% MoM; +19.4% vs 2026 Avg excl. Jul baseline).Top-of-funnel reach — healthy and growing.
First Visits / TrialsClients attending a first class: 153 (+50.0% MoM; -7.3% YoY).How much of the pipeline physically experiences the studio.
Trial Conversion (retention view)Trialists returning/converting ÷ first visits = 38 ÷ 153 = 24.8% (+1.6pp MoM).Template headline: does the first visit stick.
Trial-to-Conversion (CRM strict)Trialling leads who bought ÷ trialling leads = 23 ÷ 124 = 18.6% (vs 52.2% in Jul 2025).The sharpest view of the post-trial close failure.
First-Visit Conversion (new-client registers)First-time visitors buying same-cohort ÷ first visits = 25 ÷ 153 = 16.3% (vs 27.9% LY).Same-month close rate on fresh trialers.
Monthly ConversionsAll leads closed in-month (any cohort): ~188 (+49.2% MoM; +59.3% YoY) — a record.Desk throughput — record volume, but see value metric below.
Conversion Value (in-month cohort)Avg LTV of leads closed in-month: ₹1,483 (-85.8% YoY vs ₹10,461).Quality of what’s being closed — volume on the cheapest products.
New-Client Expected LTVForward value of converted newcomers: ₹10,387 (-67.6% YoY vs ₹32,019).Long-run worth of newly acquired clients — cohorts are shallower.
Conversion SpeedMean lead-create → first purchase: 44.8 days (+67.6% YoY vs 26.7).Follow-up urgency; every idle week cools intent.
Lead-Source ConversionConversions ÷ leads by channel: call 44.4% (9→3) · referral 27.8% (18→5) · WhatsApp 26.3% (19→5) · Hosted ~2.5% (78→2).Where marketing rupees become members vs where they evaporate.

Historical Renewal BaselineLong-run renewals ÷ resolved contracts = 4,519 ÷ 7,438 = 60.8% (39.2% lapse).Bandra’s chronic churn DNA — the structural bar to beat.
Active Risk TiersFlagged from frequency, cancels & milestones on the active register: 78 High + 24 Medium of 194 = 52.6% at risk.Next month’s churn, visible in advance — outreach list.
Behavioural Risk ThresholdsLapsed avg 2.15 sessions vs renewed 5.72; risk freq 0.5–0.8 classes/wk; class-7 milestone (10 stuck); discounted renewal 74.5% vs 58.8% full-price.The measurable moments where retention is won or lost.
